panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Gross autopsy heart from a patient whose article title identifies Friedreich's ataxia cardiomyopathy as the first manifestation; caption describes pale left heart and right ventricular dilation, a cardiac manifestation of FA. No vocabulary key matches the gross appearance, so findings are proposed. B: H&E histology showing myocardial replacement by fibrosis in a Friedreich's ataxia patient; matches vocabulary finding friedreich_ataxia_myocardial_fibrosis. C: Masson's trichrome histology showing fibrosis (blue) replacing myocardium in a Friedreich's ataxia patient; matches friedreich_ataxia_myocardial_fibrosis. D: Perls Prussian blue histology showing iron deposition in cardiac fibers in a Friedreich's ataxia patient; matches friedreich_ataxia_myocardial_iron_deposition.

panels.figure_caption: A – Gross view of the heart, showing the pale appearance of the left heart and dilation of the right ventricle. (B, C, and D, photomicrographs of the heart.). B – Myocardial replacement by fibrosis (H&E, 100X optical magnification OM). C – Remaining myocardiocytes showed in red and fibrosis replacing myocardium in blue (Masson's Trichrome Stain 40X OM). D – The blue spots indicate iron storage in the cardiac fibers (Perls Prussian Blue Stain, 400X OM).

Examination of the valves and coronaries showed no changes. Microscopic examination showed significant myocardial replacement with fibrosis (Figures 11C) and a mural thrombus at the tip of the left ventricle. B: M-mode diaphragm ultrasound in Friedreich ataxia; caption states the respiratory waves are decreased, supporting reduced diaphragmatic excursion. in_text_mentions: he indices of the diaphragm with a sector transducer(2–5MHz). Diaphragm movements were recorded within the B-Mode. For navigation, ultrasound beams were placed midclavicular into the subcostal space to visualize the diaphragm vertically and switched to M mode. The angle of the probe was adjusted so that the ultrasound beam was perpendicular to the posterior third of the right hemidiaphragm. The procedure started at the end of normal expiration and allowed subjects to inhale calmly. Measurement of diaphragm thickness and excursion with ultrasonography is shown in Figures 1A and 1B respectively.
